description: The episode list, as rows: the headless form of the reviewer's main list, so a script or a CI step can assert what the rail shows (ADR-006 §6.7). Owner: `reco-11b`.

episodes.description: One row per episode the filters selected, in `page.order`, at most `page.limit` of them. The columns are the rail's: identity, time, authorship, size, path count, review state and harness turn.

attribution_agent.description: The agent the evidence named, when it named exactly one. `null` when it did not: a name Fathom made up would outlive the correction (`e4.1`).

attribution_source.description: Which class of evidence decided the author kind — `correction`, `harness`, `trailer`, `declared`, `author`, `committer`, `message`, `identity` — or `null` when the row was written before the column existed.

author_confidence.description: The store's own confidence figure, passed through: `fathom analyze` on the same episode prints this same number, and a list that re-scaled or elided a 0.0 would be a second reality. `fathom attribution list` prints the evidence beside it.

author_kind.description: How Fathom classified the author. `unknown` is an answer, not a gap: it means the evidence did not decide.

boundary_confidence.description: How much to trust the rule that opened this episode, as the store recorded it (ADR-003 §4.7).

boundary_rule.description: Which rule opened this episode (ADR-003 §4.7), or `null`. A boundary a human drew and a boundary a heuristic guessed are different claims, which is why this is printed.

created.description: `created_utc_ms` in the shape the text report prints: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC`.

created_utc_ms.description: When the episode began, unix epoch milliseconds (ADR-004 §4.1 — the store keeps millis).

first_oid.description: The first member commit, in first-parent order.

id.description: The derived episode identity (ADR-003 §2.1) — what `fathom show`, `analyze` and `review sign` take, and what a review is keyed to.

intent_state.description: `recorded`, `digest-only`, `none`, or `null` when this build never looked — which is a different statement from 'nothing was recorded' (`e4.2`).

kind.description: `committed` for a closed episode, `provisional` for the still-growing tail of a session.

last.description: `last_utc_ms` rendered, which is the instant the row is sorted on.

last_utc_ms.description: The last member's author date, unix epoch milliseconds.

live.description: Whether any current commit still belongs to it (ADR-003 §6.3). `false` means the history that carried this episode was rewritten away; a sign-off on it still exists, which is why the row is printed and not hidden.

n_add.description: Lines added across the episode's commits — the `+` the rail prints.

n_binary.description: Binary files in the change, which is why the rail says `bin` instead of drawing a sparkline.

n_del.description: Lines removed, summed the same way as `n_add`.

n_files.description: The rail's file rollup: file rows summed over the episode's commits, so one file edited in three of this episode's commits counts three times. `paths` is the same fact asked as 'which files', which is why the two numbers can differ.

overridden.description: Whether a `fathom.toml` override moved one of this episode's boundaries.

paths.description: The distinct paths the episode touched (after a rename, the new path). Repository-relative, like every path this binary prints.

review_state.description: What the reviewer has done with it. `unread` covers 'no row yet' and 'a row that says unread' alike, which is the store's rule and the shell's `u` filter.

session.description: The harness session a trailer or an event named, or `null` — most human commits have none.

summary.description: The one-line subject the rail prints, verbatim: control characters are folded only in the text render, never here.

turn.description: The harness turn as the store keeps it — already session-qualified (ADR-005 §1), so this and `turn_id` are the same string whenever both exist.

turn_id.description: The session-qualified turn id, in the spelling `fathom hooks --trailer` prints (ADR-003 §18.2 D5), or `null`. Two sessions' turn 3 are `sess-7:3` and `ci-build:3`, never two things called `3`.

filter.description: The flags that narrowed the list, echoed as typed *and* as resolved. Echoed because a count a script cannot reproduce is not an assertion.

since.description: `--since` as typed, so `since: "2w"` and `since_utc_ms` are the same fact in two clocks: the flag is relative to the run, the instant is what the query used.

since_utc_ms.description: The resolved lower bound on `last_utc`, unix milliseconds; `null` when unbounded.

state.description: `--state` as typed, or `null`. Note that `unread` means 'nobody has decided', not 'the row says unread'.

text.description: The whole filter as one string, in the spelling the text report prints; empty means no filter was given.

until_utc_ms.description: The resolved exclusive upper bound on `last_utc`, unix milliseconds; `null` when unbounded.

index.description: Where these rows came from. Deliberately not `common.schema.json#/$defs/index`: this section answers 'which store, which epoch, how many episodes', which is all a list needs, and borrowing the status verbs' section would promise numbers this verb does not read.

epoch.description: The epoch the rows were read from (ADR-004 §6.3). A rebuild moves it, so a row can be tied to the run that wrote it.

episodes.description: Every episode the index holds — before the filters and before the page. `page.matched` is this number filtered, `page.returned` is that paged, and the rail's strip prints this one. They are three different questions and only agree by coincidence.

present.description: Always `true` here: a verb that could not read an index refuses rather than answering empty.

notes.description: What the rows cannot say, in the order a reader needs them: an empty answer and why, a page cut short by `--limit`, rows the filters excluded, ghosts `--include-dead` let in, a list longer than a frame can hold. The same strings the text report prints after a `!`.

page.description: The paging, stated as four numbers rather than as a shorter list: `matched` is the filter's answer, `returned` is the page's.

limit.description: `--limit` as typed, or `null` for 'every row the filters select' (`--limit 0`).

matched.description: Episodes the filters select, before paging. Assert on this one when the question is 'how many unread episodes are there'.

order.description: The store's ordering, named rather than assumed: the rail draws in this order, so a script and the shell see the same first row.

returned.description: Rows in `episodes`. Less than `matched` only when the page was cut short, and then `truncated` is true.

truncated.description: `matched` exceeded the page. `fathom index` has no such ceiling and neither does this verb: raise `--limit` or walk `--offset`.

review_counts.description: Every review state's share of the selection, always all six keys so a script can index by name without guessing which states are new. The `--state` filter itself is *not* applied here — `--kind agent --state unread` prints the whole agent split, which is the only way the count tells you what you filtered out. The six sum to `page.matched`.

root.description: `--root`, repository-relative or `~`-relative — never an absolute home path (ADR-002 §7.5).

title: fathom episodes --json

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: OK
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the list was printed — including when it is empty, because a quiet repository is an answer and not a failure

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: USAGE
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: clap rejected the command line, or a flag value named nothing: `--kind sideways`, `--state never`, `--since someday`

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: NOT_A_REPOSITORY
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: `--root` is not a git repository, or `.git` is unreadable

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: STORE_CORRUPT
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the episode read failed; the remedy is a rebuild

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: FEATURE_ABSENT
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: this binary was built without an index backend (the `minimal` CI binary)

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: INDEX_DEGRADED
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the repository has no index to list; the remedy is `fathom index`
